interaction.prompt: You carry the puck up the middle on an odd-man rush. The lone defender shades to one side. Tap the teammate with the open ice.

mc.stem: You have the puck in the middle on a 3-on-1. The lone defender shades toward your left-side teammate. Who has the best open ice?
opts: Your teammate open on the right side
Your teammate covered on the left side
The narrow gap right behind the defender

feedback.right: Yes. The lone defender cannot cover both sides — when they shade to your left teammate, the right-side teammate is wide open for the pass.
feedback.wrong: The defender already took away the left side. Forcing it there, or squeezing behind the defender, plays into them. The open ice is the right-side teammate.

tip: On an odd-man rush, move the puck to the side the lone defender left open.
why: One defender can only take one threat. Reading which side they commit to, and passing away from it, is the whole odd-man read.
